A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RL-EDA research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching renamed variants and renumbered appendices.

before.justification: V1 reports original optimization experiments on QUBO, NK, and NK3, including comparisons, ablations, and sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains original experimental results and adds NAS-Bench-101 optimization, short-budget experiments, scaling tests, and additional method comparisons.

M1.justification: The original order-invariant GRPO procedure remains, with renamed permutation notation. However, Appendices P–S introduce substantive variants: a curriculum that gradually reduces input dropout, a shared neural generator, critic-based advantages, and Gibbs sampling instead of autoregressive generation. Parameter sharing was only suggested as a possible extension in v1.

E1.justification: V2 extends evaluation beyond the retained synthetic QUBO, NK, and NK3 problems to NAS-Bench-101 neural architecture search. Appendix O evaluates mixed binary/categorical architecture configurations, including invalid configurations, adding a substantially different application and search environment.

E2.justification: V2 removes the explicit one-flip Tabu Search comparator, reducing the stated main comparison suite from 504 to 503 competitors. It also adds targeted comparisons against critic-based and Gibbs-sampling alternatives in Appendices Q and S, and comparative timing against BOA and CMApara in Table 3. The original PBIL, MIMIC, BOA, and Nevergrad comparisons otherwise remain.

E3.justification: Original default settings remain, but v2 adds substantial experimental protocols: 1,000-evaluation comparisons, Fast-RL-EDA with population 5 and 100 training epochs, critic scaling-parameter searches, and epoch/Gibbs-iteration sweeps. A much larger NK experiment is also introduced; its size is inconsistently reported as 1,024 in Section 4.2/Figure 19 and 1,028 in Appendix R.

E4.justification: V1's dropout, interaction-graph, population-size, KL-penalty, and network-depth analyses are retained. V2 adds training-epoch sensitivity, short-budget and curriculum analyses, a critic ablation, parameter-sharing and scaling comparisons, and a Gibbs-sampling ablation. These test previously unexamined design choices and failure conditions.

E5.justification: The retained experiments still use 10 instances with 10 independent restarts, standard-deviation bands, and two-sample t-tests with the same thresholds. New experiments extend these reporting practices; changed significance markers and additional result rows do not establish a new statistical procedure or increased replication of existing experiments.

E6.justification: V2 adds extensive NAS, short-budget, runtime, critic, shared-generator, and Gibbs-sampling results. All 42 main-table RL-EDA scores remain unchanged, but rankings and significance markers change after Tabu's removal: NK with n=128, K=8 retains 0.7369 while moving from rank 2/505 to 1/504. Figure 2 also replaces the NK n=256 panel with n=128 results, rather than showing a same-setting improvement.

T1.justification: Appendix E revises the combinatorial coefficients in the permutation-averaged likelihood and introduces the general subset weight (k-1)!(n-k)!/n!. It replaces the earlier claim that fully conditioned terms receive much smaller weights with a qualified statement about decreasing weights up to n/2. Appendix L.2 adds time and space complexity reasoning. The existing PPO derivations and convergence argument are substantially retained.

C1.justification: The central claims about order-invariant neural EDAs, structural regularization, and sample-efficient optimization remain. V2 makes the methodological contributions more explicit in the introduction and extends the conclusion from synthetic-benchmark robustness to practical applicability supported by neural architecture search.

C2.justification: V2 substantially expands discussion of applicability and limitations. It explains short-budget weakness through the diversity/convergence tradeoff, attributes poor large-instance performance of the original generator to insufficient capacity, and discusses critic scale sensitivity and computational cost. It also interprets the shared-generator and Gibbs results, providing new explanations of when particular designs help or fail.

D1.justification: V2 documents the shared generator's two 100-neuron hidden layers, critic architecture and tuning grid, curriculum settings, and NAS encoding and invalid-configuration handling. Table 3 expands CPU/GPU timing information across sizes and methods; the reported single-instance n=128 CPU time changes from 9 to 11.5 minutes. These additions substantially expand implementation and resource information beyond v1's existing defaults and software/hardware descriptions.

R1.justification: The introduction newly distinguishes generation-order invariance from the solution-space symmetries used by Sym-NCO and POMO. V2 adds their citations and the NAS-Bench-101 reference, while removing several Tabu-related references and the structured-dropout citation. The broader positioning relative to EDAs, Bayesian optimization, and autoregressive models remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 rewrites part of the introduction into an explicit contribution list, corrects the expansion of GRPO, and clarifies generation/training-order notation. It reorganizes reproducibility and end-matter statements and adds an LLM usage declaration. Most retained methodological and theoretical prose remains closely matched; the additional scientific sections do not amount to a wholesale narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: V2 changes the main paper to a two-column conference layout and extensively reflows figures and tables. It adds a generation/training diagram, comparative runtime and variant-result tables, and NAS, epoch-sensitivity, curriculum, scaling, and Gibbs plots. Existing displays are also renamed, renumbered, or relocated; the NAS curve appears in both the main text and appendix.

improvement.justification: V2 addresses important gaps in v1's validation: it adds an application beyond synthetic landscapes and directly investigates budget limitations, scalability, and alternative design choices. Appendices O–S and the comparative runtime table substantially improve assessment of practical usefulness and failure conditions. Removing the strong Tabu comparator weakens comparative coverage, and the large-instance size inconsistency remains, but the broader validation and diagnostic evidence provide a substantial net improvement.
